Existing methods can achieve satisfactory performance through carefully designed network architectures. However, they often ignore the semantic information of scene structures, leading to poor performance in the se- mantic boundary areas of the predicted depth maps. To address this issue, we propose SSRDepth, a monocular depth estimation method that leverages semantic segmentation to improve metric depth prediction.

Conclusion In this paper, we propose SSRDepth, a monocular depth estimation framework leverages semantic segmentation to improve metric depth prediction. The framework decomposes the metric depth estimation task into two parts: segmentation scale prediction through the Segmenta- tion Proposal Scale (SPS) module and semantic-aware relative depth estimation through the Adaptive Relative Depth (ARD) module. Addi- tionally, the framework includes the Segmentation Query Guided Ag- gregation (SQGA) module, which is designed to recover the structural information of local semantic segments. As the first work bridging these two domains, we provide an in-depth analysis of how these choices affect evaluation. Depth de-normalization refers to the pro- cess of transforming the model’s predicted depth values back to the GT distribution for metric evaluation. The typical de- normalization strategies include: ❶No operation: Models predict metric depth [23]:D eval =D pred. ❷ Median Alignment: Models predict SI Depth [ 15], which can be recovered by scaling the ratio of the median of the GT depth to the median of the predicted depth: Deval =D pred · median(DGT )/median(Dpred). ❸ Least-Squares (LSQ) Alignment: Models predict SSI Depth [ 25], which can be recovered by affine transformation (scaled and shifted) to best fit the GT depth. In summary, our main contributions are as follows: • We propose a novel monocular depth estimation framework- SSRDepth, which decomposes metric depth into segmentation scale and semantic-aware relative depth. Ultimately, the multiplication of these two components yields accurate metric depth. • Our proposed SQGA module employs a new feature interaction pat- tern, combined with the binary masks of semantic segments gener- ated by our designed SMG, ensuring the eﬀectiveness of multi-scale semantic feature aggregation and the recovery of structural regular- ities within semantic segments. • Our proposed SPS module predicts segmentation scale with ex- plicit constraints, allowing the model to preserve sharp semantic boundaries. The ARD module predicts semantic-aware relative depth within a normalized depth space using a hybrid regression approach, providing the necessary foundation for the prediction of metric depth.

In CutDepth, the coordinates (l,u ) and size (w,h ) of the cut re- gion are randomly chosen. However, we believe that the ver- tical and horizontal directions should not be regarded equally for depth estimation based on the following discovery. A pre- vious study [Dijk and Croon, 2019] suggested that the depth estimation networks mainly use vertical position in the im- age rather than apparent size or texture to predict the depth of arbitrary obstacles. This motivates us to proposevertical Cut- Depth, which enhances the original CutDepth by preserving the vertical geometric information. selected_chunks.text: Contents lists available at ScienceDirect Pattern Recognition journal homepage: www.elsevier.com/locate/pr SSRDepth: Combining semantic segmentation and relative depth for monocular metric depth estimation Yuhang Zou, Xiaoming Chen, Zhangyan Zhao ∗, Chenghua Zhang, Haipeng Liu School of Transportation and Logistics Engineering, Wuhan University of Technology, Wuhan, 430063, Hubei, China a r t i c l e i n f o Keywords: Monocular depth estimation Semantic segment Relative depth Masked transformer a b s t r a c t Monocular depth estimation is a pivotal task in computer vision, aimed to predict a dense depth map from a single image. Existing methods can achieve satisfactory performance through carefully designed network architectures. However, they often ignore the semantic information of scene structures, leading to poor performance in the se- mantic boundary areas of the predicted depth maps. To address this issue, we propose SSRDepth, a monocular depth estimation method that leverages semantic segmentation to improve metric depth prediction.

SSRDepth consists of an Image Encoder, a Pixel Decoder, and the Segmentation Query Guided Aggregation module (SQGA), Segmentation Proposal Scale module (SPS), and Adaptive Relative Depth module (ARD) that we propose. Additionally, we propose the segmentation proposal scale alignment loss (𝑆𝑃 𝑆𝐴 ) and introduce a multi-scale supervision strategy to further enhance model performance. 3. The proposed method In this section, we ﬁrst introduce the overall architecture of SSRDepth (Section 3. 1). Then, we present the key components of SSRDepth: the Segmentation Query Guided Aggregation module (Section 3. 2), the Segmentation Proposal Scale module (Section 3. 3), and the Adaptive Relative Depth module (Section 3. 4). 3. 1. Framework overview As shown in Fig. 2, given an input image 𝐼 ∈ ℝ3×𝐻×𝑊 , we ﬁrst extract image features through the Image Encoder and then decode them into multi-scale features {𝐹𝑙}3 𝑙=1 and per-pixel representations 𝐹𝑝 ∈ ℝ𝐶× 𝐻 4 × 𝑊 4 employing the Pixel Decoder, where 𝐶 is the number of channels, and 𝐻 × 𝑊 is the resolution.

Conclusion In this paper, we propose SSRDepth, a monocular depth estimation framework leverages semantic segmentation to improve metric depth prediction. The framework decomposes the metric depth estimation task into two parts: segmentation scale prediction through the Segmenta- tion Proposal Scale (SPS) module and semantic-aware relative depth estimation through the Adaptive Relative Depth (ARD) module. Addi- tionally, the framework includes the Segmentation Query Guided Ag- gregation (SQGA) module, which is designed to recover the structural information of local semantic segments. As the first work bridging these two domains, we provide an in-depth analysis of how these choices affect evaluation. Depth de-normalization refers to the pro- cess of transforming the model’s predicted depth values back to the GT distribution for metric evaluation. The typical de- normalization strategies include: ❶No operation: Models predict metric depth [23]:D eval =D pred. ❷ Median Alignment: Models predict SI Depth [ 15], which can be recovered by scaling the ratio of the median of the GT depth to the median of the predicted depth: Deval =D pred · median(DGT )/median(Dpred). ❸ Least-Squares (LSQ) Alignment: Models predict SSI Depth [ 25], which can be recovered by affine transformation (scaled and shifted) to best fit the GT depth.
